articleTitle: IEE Colloquium on 'Engineering Managers - Managing Engineers' (Digest No.025)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Engineering Managers - Managing Engineers
IEE Colloquium on Engineering Managers - Managing Engineers
abstract: A project team should contain everyone who takes part in decisions in any area of the project. The people who are in the team should be located together so that they can concentrate on the objectives and achieve good communications. The division of work should be minimised and responsibility should be given to those who control resources.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Engineering Managers - Managing Engineers
abstract: Project management is a service function, it aims to bring together resources to achieve a stated objective. There are requirements which must be met and a customer to be satisfied at the end of the day. To ensure that these activities are carried out correctly in a timely manner certain criteria must be met and getting this right first time is a matter of quality assurance.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Engineering Managers - Managing Engineers
abstract: The author looks at the major causes of project failure with particular reference to cost. The project life cycle and the control cycle are also discussed. Establishment of a hierarchy of objectives is presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Project definition: laying the foundations of a project
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Engineering Managers - Managing Engineers
abstract: One of the most repeated causes of projects exceeding their intended delivery date and cost is poor project definition. This is a problem which appears to be only visible with hindsight as few people recognise the potential problems during the definition stage. The author suggests means by which a project engineer/manager may avoid laying the cornerstones for later project problems. The model assumes a project engineer working in the projects division of a large company, with the responsibility of defining the users/operations departments requirements and procuring the facilities to satisfy these requirements.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Engineering Managers - Managing Engineers
abstract: A project manager must be able to tell his superiors what is likely to occur in the future in the area for which he is responsible and to quantify the probability of that occurrence. He must also be able to control the system for which he is responsible so as to eliminate unnecessary shortfalls and maximise the return in whatever way is appropriate. The author concludes that a deterministic planning system can be used for project control.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
